query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying the CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy (HEA) matrix with a minor silver addition (~5 at.% Ag) will form a temperature-adaptive, Ag-rich tribolayer that keeps the steady-state coefficient of friction (COF) ≤0.30 and lowers the specific wear rate by ≥50 % relative to the Ag-free CoCrFeNi HEA during dry sliding from room temperature up to 800 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk or thick (≥50 µm) CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy produced by vacuum arc melting and homogenized at 1100 °C for 12 h, air cooled; average grain size 10–20 µm; single-phase FCC; no intentional lubricant additions.
generation.intervention: Introduce 5 atomic % Ag uniformly into the CoCrFeNi matrix (yielding CoCrFeNiAg0.05) by co-melting or co-sputtering so that Ag is supersaturated at room temperature but able to diffuse and segregate to the surface during sliding.
generation.conditions: Unlubricated (dry) reciprocating sliding against an alumina counter-body, 5 N normal load, 5 Hz, 5 mm stroke, total sliding distance 100 m, conducted in laboratory air (~20 % O₂, 30–60 % RH) at 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C, 600 °C and 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: In-situ formed, nanometre-scale, continuous Ag/Ag₂O-rich tribofilm on the wear track, underlain by an oxide-bearing nanocrystalline mechanically mixed layer (MML).
generation.mechanism: 1. At 25–400 °C, silver has high surface mobility and segregates to the sliding interface, reducing adhesive junction strength and shear strength, thus lowering COF. 2. Above ~450 °C, Ag oxidises to Ag₂O/AgO; the soft, low-shear oxide and retained metallic Ag co-form a lubricious layer that replenishes continuously from the Ag supersaturated matrix and trapped wear debris, sustaining low friction and acting as a solid lubricant. 3. The Ag-containing MML dissipates shear and accommodates strain, reducing delamination and third-body abrasion, thus lowering wear rate across the full temperature range.
generation.predicted_outcome: Mean steady-state COF ≤0.30 and specific wear rate ≤2 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ for CoCrFeNiAg0.05 at all test temperatures; baseline CoCrFeNi exhibits COF 0.6–0.8 at ≥400 °C and wear rate ≥4 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹.
generation.baseline: Ag-free CoCrFeNi HEA tested under identical conditions, historically reporting COF ≈0.4 at RT but rising to 0.6–0.8 above 400 °C, with wear rates doubling or tripling at the highest temperatures.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness requires: (a) ambient air or mildly oxidative atmospheres (pO₂ ≥10⁻³ atm); (b) loads ≤10 N (≈1 GPa Hertzian contact); (c) temperatures ≤850 °C (to limit Ag evaporation). In vacuum or inert gas, or above 850 °C, the lubricious Ag/Ag₂O layer will not form or will sublime, so performance may converge to the baseline.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of Ag sublimation above ~750 °C and its impact on long-duration tests is uncertain; grain-size dependence of Ag diffusion kinetics may shift the optimal Ag level; interaction of Ag with Cr₂O₃ or spinel oxides could either assist or hinder tribofilm continuity.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two coupons: (1) CoCrFeNi (baseline) and (2) CoCrFeNiAg0.05 (intervention) with identical surface finish (Ra ≤0.05 µm). Perform dry reciprocating sliding tests in air at 25, 200, 400, 600 and 800 °C under the specified load and stroke parameters, using a 6 mm alumina ball. Record COF continuously; measure wear track volume by 3D profilometry after each test; analyse wear tracks by XPS/EDS to confirm Ag-rich tribofilm.
measurements: Steady-state COF (average after run-in, last 80 m of sliding)
Surface chemistry and thickness of tribofilm (XPS depth profile)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, at any tested temperature, either (a) the mean steady-state COF of CoCrFeNiAg0.05 exceeds 0.30, or (b) its specific wear rate is not at least 50 % lower than that of the baseline CoCrFeNi under identical conditions.
